en.name: Mung bean sprouts
en.summary: Mung bean sprouts are a refrigerated raw food. The published figure is 4–6 weeks in the fridge, which assumes sprouts that are properly drained and kept dry in a container — but any shop pack carries its own date, usually far shorter, and that date is the one to follow.
en.pantry: Sprouts must never be left at room temperature. They are grown warm and damp, which is exactly the condition bacteria need, and they are usually eaten raw or barely cooked, so there is no cooking step to fall back on. That combination is why raw sprouts are a food safety authorities single out: cooking them through is the reliable control, and raw sprouts are not advised for pregnant people, young children, older adults or anyone immunocompromised. Out of the fridge, the two-hour rule applies, or one hour above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.fridge: Never refrigerate wet sprouts — drain them thoroughly first, then transfer them to a plastic bag or a glass or plastic container rather than leaving them sitting in water. Kept dry and cold at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, the published figure is 4–6 weeks. In practice a supermarket pack will be dated much sooner than that and you should go by the printed date; the long figure describes ideal handling, not a tub of sprouts that has already spent a warm afternoon on a market stall. Check them daily — sprouts turn quickly once they start, and one slimy handful spoils the container.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for bean sprouts, and freezing them is not worth doing. They are almost entirely water in thin, crisp cells, so freezing bursts the structure and what thaws is a limp, watery mass with none of the snap that is the whole point. If you have too many, cook them into something — a stir-fry, a soup — and store the cooked dish instead.
spoilage: Sliminess, or sprouts sticking together in a wet clump.
A sour, musty or fermented smell — fresh sprouts smell of almost nothing.
Brown, soft or mushy tips and roots.
Water pooling in the bottom of the container.
tips: Drain thoroughly before storing; wet sprouts rot from the bottom of the tub.
Follow the printed date on a shop pack over any general figure.
Cook them through if you are serving anyone vulnerable.
Pick out any that have gone soft rather than leaving them among the good ones.

faq.q: How long do mung bean sprouts keep in the fridge?
faq.a: The published figure is 4–6 weeks at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, drained and kept dry in a container. A shop pack's own date is usually much shorter and should be followed.
There is no timeline for it and little point — they thaw limp and watery. Cook them and store the dish instead.

faq.q: Are raw bean sprouts safe to eat?
faq.a: They are a recognised raw-food risk because they are grown warm and damp. Cooking them through is the reliable control, and raw sprouts are not advised for pregnant, very young, elderly or immunocompromised people.

zh.name: 綠豆芽
zh.summary: 綠豆芽是生鮮的冷藏食品。已公布的數字是冷藏 4～6 週，那假設芽菜已經確實瀝乾、乾爽地裝在容器裡——但市售包裝都有自己的日期，通常短得多，而那個日期才是你該遵守的。
zh.pantry: 豆芽絕對不能放室溫。它是在溫暖潮濕的環境裡長出來的，而那正是細菌需要的條件；再加上它常常生食或只是快速汆燙，等於沒有「烹煮」這道防線可以倚靠。這兩件事加起來，就是各國食安機關特別點名生芽菜的原因：確實煮熟是可靠的控制手段，而孕婦、幼童、長者與免疫力低下者不建議生食芽菜。離開冰箱後適用 2 小時原則，室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。
zh.fridge: 絕對不要把濕的豆芽直接冰起來——先徹底瀝乾，再裝進塑膠袋或玻璃／塑膠容器，不要讓它泡在水裡。保持乾爽並放 4 °C 以下，公布的數字是 4～6 週。實務上超市包裝標的日期會短得多，請以包裝日期為準；那個長數字描述的是理想的處理狀況，不是一盤已經在市場攤位上待了一個悶熱下午的豆芽。請每天檢查——豆芽一旦開始壞就壞得很快，一把發黏的就會拖垮整盒。
zh.freezer: 豆芽沒有給冷凍期限，冷凍它也不划算。它幾乎全是水，裝在又薄又脆的細胞裡，冷凍會把結構脹破，解凍後只剩軟塌出水的一團，那股爽脆感——也就是吃它的全部理由——完全不見。買太多的話，就炒一盤或煮成湯，保存煮好的菜。
spoilage: 發黏，或黏成濕答答的一團。
聞起來發酸、有霉味或發酵味——新鮮豆芽幾乎沒有味道。
尖端和根部變褐、變軟、爛掉。
tips: 保存前徹底瀝乾；濕的豆芽會從盒底開始爛。
市售包裝以印的日期為準，優先於任何通則數字。
要給體質較弱的人吃，就確實煮熟。
軟掉的先挑出來丟掉，不要讓它留在好的裡面。

faq.q: 綠豆芽冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 公布的數字是 4 °C 以下、瀝乾裝盒 4～6 週。市售包裝自己的日期通常短得多，請以它為準。
沒有對應期限，也沒什麼意義——解凍後軟爛出水。不如炒熟再保存那道菜。
它是被公認的生食風險品，因為是在溫暖潮濕環境培育的。確實煮熟是可靠的控制方式；孕婦、幼童、長者與免疫力低下者不建議生食。
